site.name: greengrove
site.summary: greengrove-clone Fictional pet insurance "GreenGrove" marketing site, including a 6-step quote wizard. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing page: hand-drawn dog illustration hero + 3 value props + customer review cards + FAQ entry | | `quote.html` | 6-step quote wizard: 1 pet type (6 icon cards) / 2 breed (200+ dogs, 60+ cats, other species auto-switched ARIA combobox with searchable dropdown — keyboard up/down/Enter/Esc) / 3 age (year/month toggle + stepper) / 4 pre-existing conditions (19 chip multi-select + None toggle) / 5 three tier cards (Sprout / Sapling / Oak) + deductible dropdown + collapsible side-by-side comparison table + live per-tier quote / 6 quote summary (monthly fee + annual total + inclusions + 14-day price lock mock); top 6-step dot indicator allows jumping back; floating Back / Continue bar | | `faq.html` | 12 common-question `<details>` accordion |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full greengrove system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The core onboarding and support flows are understandable, but several interactions feel fragile or underexplained. The most consistent issue is mobile usability: header links and primary actions are repeatedly below the 44px tap-target guidance, and the FAQ accordion could not be reliably activated on mobile. The claims form is more legible than the quote wizard, but its submission feedback relies on browser-native validation and the primary submit control is also too short for comfortable touch use; a few adjacent areas remain untested, especially quote-step progression and claims upload feedback.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore GreenGrove’s primary quote/onboarding flow, then validate adjacent informational and claims paths, with special attention to step navigation, conditional inputs, summary correctness, and mobile tap-target issues.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the marketing landing page to confirm the main conversion entry points and then drive deep through the 6-step quote wizard, exercising each step’s visible controls and any branching behaviors. After the quote flow, validate recovery/navigation patterns via the step indicator and Back/Continue controls, then inspect the claims form and FAQ accordion as adjacent support flows. Repeat the critical quote and landing-page checks in a mobile viewport, paying attention to the small-tap-target warnings already seen on the top navigation.
assumptions: The quote wizard is the main product flow and can be completed without authentication or external dependencies.
The visible 6-step structure on quote.html reflects the full set of core onboarding states, including the summary and rate-lock dialog/state.
The claims page submits as a local demo form and may not require real file upload validation beyond visible control behavior.
FAQ content is implemented as plain <details> accordions and should be expandable/collapsible without additional data loading.
risk_hotspots: quote.html step 2 breed selector: ARIA combobox/searchable dropdown with keyboard up/down/Enter/Esc behavior
quote.html step 3 age controls: year/month toggle and stepper edge cases
quote.html step 4 conditions: 19-chip multi-select plus None toggle interaction conflicts
quote.html step 5 tier selection: Sprout/Sapling/Oak cards, deductible dropdown, and collapsible comparison table
quote.html step 6 quote summary and 'Rate locked!' dialog/state: pricing consistency and lock messaging
quote.html top 6-step dot indicator and floating Back/Continue bar: skipping, recovery, and state persistence
index.html header/navigation tap targets: several controls are below mobile guidance
claims.html submit claim form: required-field handling, date/file input behavior, and submission feedback

phases.title: Landing page entry and mobile sanity
phases.objective: Validate the marketing entry point, primary quote CTA, supporting links, and the mobile usability risk already flagged on the header navigation.
key_checks: Open the hero CTA 'Start a free quote' and confirm it lands on the quote wizard.
Open the FAQ teaser link and confirm it lands on FAQ content.
Check the header links for Claims and FAQ, and note whether Sign in is inert or placeholder.
Repeat the same navigation checks in a mobile viewport and verify the small tap targets are still usable.
exit_criteria: Quote, FAQ, and Claims navigation have each been reached at least once from the landing page.
The mobile viewport has reproduced the header tap-target issue or confirmed the controls remain operable despite the warning.

phases.title: Quote wizard core path
phases.objective: Exercise the full onboarding flow from step 1 through step 6, validating the default path and the main state transitions.
key_checks: Select each pet type option enough to confirm the step reacts correctly and Continue enables progression.
Advance through the wizard in order and verify each step title/state updates correctly.
Check that the step dots and floating Back/Continue bar move the user predictably through the flow.
At the summary step, verify the displayed monthly fee, annual total, inclusions, and 14-day price lock messaging.
exit_criteria: The run has reached the final quote summary state at least once.
All six steps have been visited in a normal forward flow.

phases.title: Quote wizard branching and edge states
phases.objective: Stress the controls that are most likely to have complex logic, conditional rendering, or keyboard accessibility issues.
key_checks: Use the breed combobox/search dropdown with keyboard navigation, selection, and escape/cancel behavior.
Toggle age between year and month and test the stepper for minimum/maximum or boundary behavior.
Select several condition chips, then test the None toggle and confirm mutual exclusivity or reset behavior.
Pick different tier cards and change the deductible dropdown to see if quote values update consistently.
Open and close the comparison table if present, ensuring it reflects the selected tier/deductible.
exit_criteria: At least one non-default state has been exercised for steps 2, 3, 4, and 5.
Any dynamic quote recalculation or summary update has been observed and compared across selections.

phases.title: Recovery, navigation, and persistence
phases.objective: Validate that users can jump back, recover from mistakes, and retain or reset state sensibly across the wizard.
key_checks: Use the 6-step dot indicator to jump backward and forward, checking whether earlier choices persist.
Use the floating Back button from later steps and confirm it returns to the expected prior step.
Change an earlier choice after reaching a later step and verify downstream values update or invalidate appropriately.
Test whether the Continue button is blocked when required inputs are missing or contradictory.
exit_criteria: At least one backward navigation path and one non-linear step-jump path have been validated.
The flow’s handling of edited prior answers has been observed.

phases.title: Claims form and FAQ support flows
phases.objective: Cover the adjacent support pages for form behavior and disclosure patterns outside the quote wizard.
key_checks: On claims.html, inspect required-field behavior for pet name, date, reason, amount, and invoice upload.
Attempt a submission with missing or partial fields to see validation and feedback behavior.
Exercise the invoice input with both image/PDF selection paths if possible.
On faq.html, expand and collapse multiple <details> items to confirm accordion behavior and readability.
exit_criteria: The claims form has been tested for visible validation and submission behavior.
Multiple FAQ items have been expanded and collapsed successfully.

phases.title: Mobile regression pass on critical interactions
phases.objective: Repeat the most important conversion and support checks under mobile viewport constraints, emphasizing touch usability.
key_checks: Re-test the landing-page CTA and top navigation on mobile for tap-target usability.
Walk at least the quote wizard entry and one deeper quote step on mobile to check whether the workflow remains usable.
Open the claims form and verify the input stack and submit control are still operable on a narrow viewport.
Confirm FAQ accordions remain easy to expand on mobile.
exit_criteria: Critical entry and form controls have been checked in mobile viewport.
Any mobile-specific usability regressions have been noted against the desktop behavior.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 4 known HTML pages: index.html, quote.html, claims.html, faq.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the primary CTA path, all 6 quote steps, the quote wizard’s branching controls, the claims form fields/upload, and multiple FAQ accordion items.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the landing-page navigation, quote entry and at least one deep wizard interaction, plus claims and FAQ interaction checks in mobile viewport.

notes: The prescan already shows no console or network errors, so prioritize interaction correctness and state handling over infrastructure issues.
Small tap targets on the landing-page header are the clearest documented accessibility risk and should be explicitly rechecked on mobile.
Use the quote wizard’s summary as the main point for comparing whether earlier selections materially affect pricing and lock messaging.

findings.user_goal: Reach support content and navigate between pages on a phone without mis-taps.
findings.problem: The global header repeatedly uses very small tap targets on mobile, making core navigation hard to use comfortably.
findings.evidence: On the mobile claims page, GreenGrove is 135x28px, Get a quote is 73x22px, Claims is 44x22px, and FAQ is 28x22px; the same pattern appears across the FAQ and index pages in the trajectory and layout warnings.
findings.why_it_matters: When primary navigation is hard to tap, users are more likely to miss destinations or abandon the flow, especially on small screens.
findings.suggestion: Increase header hit areas to at least 44px tall and add padding around text links so the nav is easier to tap on mobile.
findings.source_hint: claims.html header nav / faq.html header nav

findings.user_goal: Open FAQ answers on mobile to get help without leaving the page.
findings.problem: The FAQ accordion is not behaving like a reliable tap target on mobile; repeated clicks on question rows timed out and no answer content appeared.
findings.evidence: Steps 77–79 on faq.html show click failures for ux-5 and ux-8, with the page remaining on a collapsed list of questions and no answer text revealed; the recent trajectory notes that the disclosure was not operable from these taps.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot expand help content, the FAQ page becomes a dead end instead of a support resource.
findings.suggestion: Enlarge the accordion row hit area, verify the entire question row is clickable, and provide a clear expanded/collapsed state change when opened.

findings.user_goal: Submit a claim from mobile with confidence that the main action is easy to activate.
findings.problem: The primary 'Submit claim' button is visually present but too short for comfortable touch interaction.
findings.evidence: Final observation flags the submit button at 292x39px on mobile, below the 44px guidance; earlier observations also repeatedly noted the submit control as a small tap target.
findings.why_it_matters: A cramped submit button increases mis-taps and makes the form feel less trustworthy and less polished on phones.
findings.suggestion: Increase the button height to 44px or more and add spacing above/below it so the final action is easy to hit.

findings.user_goal: Understand what happens when a required claim field is missing after submission.
findings.problem: Claim submission relies on browser-native validation with a generic tooltip instead of clearer inline feedback, so the error state is not very instructive.
findings.evidence: When the form was submitted incomplete, the browser showed 'Please fill out this field.' and focus landed on the first missing field (e.g., Pet name or Visit date), with no custom inline error messaging or broader explanation.
findings.why_it_matters: Generic browser messaging can be easy to miss and may not explain what to fix next, especially for multi-field forms.
findings.suggestion: Add inline field-level errors and a brief summary near the submit button so users can quickly see what is missing and why.

findings.user_goal: Continue through the quote wizard after choosing a pet type.
findings.problem: Step 1 of the quote flow does not clearly explain why Continue is inert when no pet is selected, and the attempted pet-card interactions did not produce visible selection feedback.
findings.evidence: On quote.html, the screen shows six pet-type cards and a Continue button, but clicks on a pet card timed out and clicking Continue produced no URL or visible-text change; the trajectory notes no selected state or confirmation was visible.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot tell what is required before continuing, they may think the page is broken or get stuck on the first step.
findings.suggestion: Show an explicit selected state on pet cards and add a short validation hint near Continue when no option has been chosen.

findings.user_goal: Scan the claims page and understand the next action quickly.
findings.problem: The claims page is structurally clear, but the hierarchy is dominated by instructional copy above the form, which pushes the actual action lower on the screen.
findings.evidence: The mobile claims page opens with several informational cards and explanatory sentences before the fields and submit action; the final screenshot shows the submit button near the lower part of the viewport with additional fields still above it.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may have to scan more than necessary before finding the actual input path, especially on small screens where content is already tightly packed.
findings.suggestion: Condense the introductory copy or visually separate it from the form so the first required field and submit path stand out more quickly.

gaps: 15 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
43% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
